mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC improved net +3.7 points over the last four weeks, with the largest single-week gain (+4.1 points) occurring most recently, indicating self-reinforcing recovery momentum as consumers resume shopping routines. This momentum is expected to persist, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean fails to exceed its trailing 28-day mean, indicating the recent momentum reversed rather than continued.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT improved from -38.6 to -29.6 over the snapshot window, crossing above -30 in the most recent week. This signals renewed commuter-linked foot traffic that drives incidental retail stops near transit hubs, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -38.6 to -29.6, crossing -30 in the final observed week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks following TRANSIT's crossing above -30, or TRANSIT reverses below -35.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are recovering simultaneously (-36.9 to -30.4 and -32.7 to -29.6 respectively), creating a compounding effect where commuters both travel more and work more in-person, generating additional incidental shopping trips beyond what either series alone would predict, boosting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together than the sum of their individual expected effects, falsifying the interaction term.
